title:
Comment of Hunter Keys in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/28/2026

documents.name: 151857.txt
documents.text:
Hunter Keys, Hogansville, GA.
I am writing in opposition to the proposed data center in the Cook Inlet. I work as a nurse practitioner in remote Alaska Native American villages, and have the privilege of visiting communities around the region. I can attest to the beauty and grandeur of the natural environment here as well as the strength of the people. In my travels, I can attest that what people need is NOT a data center but stronger protections against this very problem: corporations from outside the state that seek to raid, extract and profit off of Alaska’s natural resources, threatening if not outright harming the ecosystem and ripping apart the fabric of local economies and communities. Just a quick look at this proposal confirms this tendency: a corporation with no ties to the state seeking to make money from Federal contracts, all at the expense of the natural and human environment here.

Data centers (and AI more broadly) pose a unique danger to local communities and beyond; the Cook Inlet is a fragile ecosystem that deserves better from our elected representatives and the business community. 

Far more energy and attention should be spent on protecting this magnificent part of the world, investing in local economies, and building more resilient infrastructure for the coming future.
